assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: bug (a trace exists; the daemon discards it -- see below)
driver_capability: ready (but no existing mock is wire-compatible; record must build one -- see recipe)
route: record-known-failing

## Reasoning

### agent = yes -- not inferred, directly captured

Muse's Meta-provider client retries a failed model call with backoff and, when a retry succeeds, the turn completes normally. This is not a doc guess or a synthetic elicitation: scanning every session.jsonl under ~/.local/share/muse/sessions on this machine (`find ~/.local/share/muse/sessions -name session.jsonl`, this assessment) surfaced a REAL, naturally-occurring example inside session `01a09c47-506a-7763-b82a-9ab89a9e195a` (task_id `01a09c50-27eb-7e83-ac0e-d19d69bdade4`, run_id `a16767b1-dd74-401e-99e4-570b613dc6aa`), a complete, ordered task lifecycle:

```
proposed -> accepted -> scheduled -> side_effect_intent -> started
status{phase:"opening_stream", facets:[{kind:"external_attempt",attempt:1,max_attempts:10}]}
status{phase:"retry_scheduled", facets:[{kind:"external_attempt",attempt:1,next_attempt:2,max_attempts:10,retry_delay_ms:5000,error_kind:"rate_limited",http_status:429}]}
status{phase:"opening_stream", facets:[{kind:"external_attempt",attempt:2,max_attempts:10}]}
status{phase:"stream_succeeded", facets:[{kind:"external_attempt",attempt:2,max_attempts:10,error_kind:"stream_succeeded"}]}
completed
```

A sibling example in the same session (task_id `01a09c52-0c50-7fa1-ae9f-f3da7bc7a75a`) shows the identical shape, and a third (task_id `01a09c58-...`) shows the same mechanism triggered by `http_status:504`/`error_kind:"server"` instead of 429 -- confirming the retry mechanism is general to "the provider call failed transiently" (rate limiting AND 5xx), matching scenario 2.22's own "HTTP 529 overloaded_error OR any transient overload" framing rather than being 429-specific. A full scan of every local session.jsonl found 1881 `kind:"task"`,`event.kind:"status"` records total and at least 5 genuine `phase:"retry_scheduled"` examples (`python3` scan, this assessment, command available in caveats). The owning RUN's own `started`/`terminal` events for this run_id carry ZERO trace of any of this (checked directly: `terminal:"cancelled"` for unrelated reasons much later, no attempt/retry field anywhere) -- the retry signal lives ONLY in the task-level status trail, confirming this is a genuinely separate channel from what the parser currently reads.

### daemon = bug -- a trace exists, and the daemon already has the exact consumer built for it

**The trace.** `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go`'s `parseSessionEnvelope` (~line 250-264) dispatches `kind:"run"` and `kind:"approval"` explicitly and Skip=true's every other `kind` in its `default` arm, whose own comment enumerates `kind:"task"`'s full `event.kind` vocabulary including `"status"` by name. The package doc (lines 57-74) justifies discarding `kind:"task"` ENTIRELY as tool-call deduplication (`assistant_tool_calls_committed`/`tool_result_batch_committed` already cover tool calls without needing the lower-level `task`/`tool_batch.effect.*` view) -- a sound rationale for TOOL calls, but the retry-scheduled status records above are `task_kind:"model.meta.response"` MODEL-call bookkeeping, a different semantic class the package doc never addresses. `parser_test.go`'s `TestParseLine_TaskKindEvents_Skipped` (~line 508) locks the blanket Skip=true, but its fixture is a `side_effect_intent` tool-call example -- the lock was never exercised against a `status`/`retry_scheduled` record, so nothing here contradicts today's tests; it simply shows the blanket rule's net is wider than its stated justification. `muse schema generate-json-schema --out <dir>` (run live on this machine, muse-bin 1.2.1-R2847.1) independently corroborates from the wire side: `turn/retryScheduled`'s `TurnRetryScheduledParams` (`msp.schema.json`) is described as "observable mid-turn, non-terminal", carries `attempt`/`maxAttempts`/`nextAttempt`/`retryDelayMs`/`reason`, and its `sourceRange` field is documented as "the durable record this event folded from (the session stream's mirror of the retry-scheduled task status)" -- i.e. muse's own protocol documentation says the wire notification is projected FROM the exact on-disk record this assessment captured directly.

**The consumer already exists, built for a different adapter.** `core/pkg/tailer/parser.go`'s `SessionError` struct already carries `Attempt *int`, `MaxAttempts *int`, `RetryIn *time.Duration`, `HTTPStatus *int` (~line 371-379) and `ErrorPhase` (`ErrorPhaseUnknown`/`ErrorPhaseRetrying`/`ErrorPhaseTerminal`, ~line 343-349) -- fields that map almost 1:1 onto the captured record's `attempt`/`max_attempts`/`retry_delay_ms`/`http_status`. `core/domain/session/session_error.go`'s doc for `ErrorPhaseRetrying` (~line 44-46) states plainly: "The session is failing but not yet lost, and the informative behaviour is to sit red for the whole retry window rather than flicker per attempt" and the type's top comment explicitly names "#1803's provider-overloaded-retry and provider-overloaded-terminal scenarios" as the reason it exists. `SessionError.ClearedByTurnBoundary()` (`core/pkg/tailer/parser.go` ~line 412-414) fires ONLY when `Phase == ErrorPhaseRetrying`, with the doc explaining: "A retrying error is the one shape where a turn boundary genuinely means recovery... That is what makes provider-overloaded-retry end green rather than staying red forever." `core/application/services/state_classifier.go`'s `session_error` rule paints the session `error` the instant `SessionError != nil` (muse declares no hooks, so this rule -- and `classifyAgentDone`'s independent, converging check -- both fire unconditionally). So the daemon-side machinery for EXACTLY this scenario is already built, tested (for claudecode), and sitting idle for muse -- what's missing is a ~10-line addition to `parser.go`'s task-kind handling: when `event.kind=="status"` AND `task_kind=="model.meta.response"` (or simply any task) AND `details.phase=="retry_scheduled"`, set `ev.SessionError = &tailer.SessionError{Phase: ErrorPhaseRetrying, Class: facet.error_kind, HTTPStatus: facet.http_status, Attempt: facet.attempt, MaxAttempts: facet.max_attempts, RetryIn: facet.retry_delay_ms}`. I did not make this change -- assess is doc+code research, not a fix -- but the fix is precisely scoped and low-risk, which is why I judge `bug` (a mishandled, spec-required observable) rather than `incapable`.

**Why this is `bug` and not `incapable`.** The evidence rule requires a concrete citation for either verdict. `incapable` means no trace exists / the 3-state model can't represent it -- neither is true here: the trace is captured verbatim above, and the daemon's own domain model (`ErrorPhaseRetrying`) was purpose-built to represent exactly this shape. `bug` means a trace exists that the daemon mishandles, which is what the parser's blanket `default: Skip=true` does to it.

### Contrast with claudecode's 2-22 (frozen, `daemon=incapable`) -- a genuinely different root cause, not a copy-paste mismatch

`replaydata/agents/claudecode/scenarios/2-22_provider-overloaded-retry/metadata.json` is `daemon_capability:"incapable"`, LIVE-MEASURED across four real recordings against `mock-anthropic-error`: on claude-code 2.1.243/2.1.245 the retry ladder is rendered to the TUI only and genuinely NEVER written to the transcript at all (a version regression from 2.1.143, which DID persist it -- see that cell's `2-9_token-quota-exhausted` citation). That is a true `untraced`/`incapable` case: the agent has the feature, but exercising it leaves zero trace in any Source the adapter reads, on the CURRENT binary. Muse's situation is structurally different: the trace is not merely theorized to exist -- it is sitting in this machine's real session.jsonl files right now, in exactly the shape needed. The two cells reaching different pillar verdicts under superficially similar scenario names is not an inconsistency; it reflects two different agents' actual on-disk behavior, each independently measured.

### driver = ready, but no existing mock is wire-compatible -- a genuine, named prerequisite

`replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh` already reads `base_url` out of `$SETTINGS_PATH` (`jq -r '.base_url // empty'`, ~line 113-114) and `spawn_muse_repl` appends `--base-url "$BASE_URL"` (~line 277) -- ported while landing the 2-14 sibling, confirmed by direct read (not assumed). `DRIVE_ELICITS` already covers `send`/`wait_turn`/`sleep`/`exit_clean`, everything this recipe's script needs. So the driver SCRIPT primitive set is complete: `driver_capability: ready`.

What is missing is a MOCK, not a driver step type. Muse's `--provider` flag only accepts `echo|meta` (`muse --help`, run live on this machine) -- `--base-url` redirects the SAME Meta-protocol client to a different host, it does not change what wire protocol muse speaks. Muse's Meta client POSTs to `/responses` (confirmed directly: the 2-14 sibling's live dead-port failure text reads `"...url (http://127.0.0.1:18799/responses)..."`, and this assessment's live captures show `producer.detail.stream.last_wire_event_type:"response.completed"`, an OpenAI-Responses-API-shaped SSE event name). Grepping every existing mock's registered routes (`tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-{anthropic-429,anthropic-5xx,anthropic-error,openai-429,gemini-429,gemini-5xx}/main.go`): `mock-anthropic-*` serve `/v1/messages`; `mock-openai-429` serves `/v1/chat/completions` + `/v1/models`; `mock-gemini-*` serve Gemini's path shapes. None serves `/responses`. Pointing muse's `--base-url` at any of them would 404 against that mock's own catch-all handler -- untested, and not obviously representative of an overload (muse might classify a 404 as non-retryable and give up early, which would misrepresent the scenario). CRUCIALLY, unlike the 2-14/2-23 siblings (which only need the provider call to fail PERMANENTLY, so a dead port -- pure connection refusal, always fails -- is a perfectly good elicitation), this scenario needs the provider call to fail N times and then SUCCEED. A dead port cannot structurally produce that: nothing is listening, so it never succeeds. `record` must build a new, stateful mock (a `/responses` handler returning HTTP 429/5xx for the first N requests, then a valid streamed completion) before this cell is recordable -- named precisely as a recipe precondition below, not folded into the driver-pillar verdict, per the assess skill's own framing ("a mock" is explicitly one of the prereq categories, distinct from a driver step-type gap).

## RE-ASSESSMENT (2026-09-14) -- both blockers closed, verdict flips to daemon=full / route=record

This is a re-assessment of the cell above, done after both named blockers were
built. Per the brief's instruction, nothing below is taken on trust -- every
claim was independently re-run or re-read on this machine.

### daemon: bug -> full, independently re-verified

Commit `10e0c6554` ("feat(muse): close four parser gaps -- task estimate,
todos, background, retry") adds `sessionKindTask` routing to
`core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go`: `parseTaskEvent` dispatches
`kind:"task"` on `event.kind=="status"`, and `parseTaskStatus` reads
`details.phase=="retry_scheduled"`, walks `details.facets[]` for the
`kind:"external_attempt"` entry, and sets
`ev.SessionError = &tailer.SessionError{Phase: ErrorPhaseRetrying, Class:
attempt.error_kind, HTTPStatus: OptInt(attempt,"http_status"), Attempt:
OptInt(attempt,"attempt"), MaxAttempts: OptInt(attempt,"max_attempts"),
RetryIn: OptDurationFromMillis(attempt,"retry_delay_ms")}` -- confirmed by
reading the diff directly (`git show 10e0c6554 --
core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go`), not by trusting the commit
message.

One correction the implementing agent made to THIS assessment's own brief: I
had proposed gating on `task_kind=="model.meta.response"`; that field is only
present on the task's earlier `proposed` event, never on the `status` record
itself, which would have required cross-event state the parser doesn't carry.
The shipped fix gates on the `external_attempt` facet's presence in the SAME
`status` record instead -- self-contained, and (per the parser's own doc
comment, corroborated independently below) matches all 86 real
`retry_scheduled` occurrences in this machine's local corpus: rate_limited/429
(68), transport (9, no http_status), server/503 (5), decode (4, no
http_status), server/504 (2). `HTTPStatus` is read via `tailer.OptInt`
(nil-safe), which is why the transport/decode kinds -- genuinely missing an
HTTP status -- don't crash or coerce to zero.

Re-ran the test suite myself: `go test
./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/... -race -count=1` is green, including
the two new tests that exercise this path directly --
`TestParseLine_TaskStatus_RetryScheduled_SetsSessionErrorRetrying` and
`TestParseLine_TaskStatus_RetryScheduled_NoHTTPStatus_NilNotZero` -- and
`TestParseLine_TaskKindEvents_Skipped`, the lock on the blanket
`kind:"task"` skip, still passes unmodified (its fixture is a
`side_effect_intent` tool-call record, a different `event.kind` than
`status`).

The clearing half was independently re-read, not assumed: `parseRunTerminal`
(`core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go` line 552) sets
`ev.EventType = "turn_done"` unconditionally on every `kind:"run"`,
`event.kind:"terminal"` record, regardless of `terminal` value. So the
eventually-successful run's own `terminal:"completed"` event is what
`core/pkg/tailer/tailer_metrics.go`'s `clearSessionErrorOnRecovery` matches
against (`parsed.EventType == "turn_done" &&
t.sessionError.ClearedByTurnBoundary()`), and `SessionError.ClearedByTurnBoundary()`
(`core/pkg/tailer/parser.go` line 412-414) returns true only for
`Phase == ErrorPhaseRetrying` -- exactly the phase `parseTaskStatus` now sets.
`core/domain/session/session_error.go`'s `ErrorPhaseRetrying` doc (line 44-46)
still reads "the informative behaviour is to sit red for the whole retry
window rather than flicker per attempt", and the mechanism was purpose-built
for this scenario, so the daemon-side story is coherent end to end, read
directly rather than inferred.

The parser fix also moved a golden: `10e0c6554`'s commit message reports
`2-13_turn-end-terminal-text`'s recording contained a naturally-occurring
retry that used to be silently dropped and now surfaces
`working->error->ready`, with that cell's invariant (forbids `waiting`, not
`error`) still holding at 4/4 -- a real behavioural change exercised outside
synthetic tests, not just a unit-test pass.

### driver/mock: the missing mock is built, independently re-verified

Commit `ecdfa5432` ("feat(onboarding): stateful /responses mock for muse
provider-overloaded-retry") adds
`tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-muse-overload/main.go`: a
`POST /responses` handler with `--status`, `--succeed-after N`,
`--ignore-substring` (default `"reminder observer"`, case-insensitive) flags.
Read the source directly: it counts only non-ignored requests, fails the
first N with the configured status, and streams a full OpenAI-Responses-API
SSE completion (`response.created` ... `response.completed`) for request
N+1 onward -- exactly the "fail N times then succeed" shape this scenario
needs and a dead port structurally cannot produce. `--succeed-after 0` is
also supported (never succeeds) for the `2-23_provider-overloaded-terminal`
sibling, confirming this mock is shared infrastructure, not single-purpose.

This addresses the exact side-channel risk the brief flagged: muse issues its
own background "skill reminder observer" `/responses` calls concurrently with
the visible turn, and a single shared counter would let those steal N-slots
from the turn under test nondeterministically. The mock's
`handleResponses` checks `--ignore-substring` BEFORE incrementing the
counter, so those calls are answered happily and never counted -- read
directly in the source, not assumed from the commit message.

Re-ran the mock's own test suite: `go test
./tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-muse-overload/... -race -count=1`
is green (`TestHandleResponses_FailsFirstNThenSucceeds`,
`TestHandleResponses_IgnoresReminderObserverSideChannel`).

Then went one step further than re-running tests: the commit message cites a
live end-to-end recording, session
`01a0a091-234a-7b42-9058-66de9fa99850`. That session directory still exists
on this machine's disk
(`~/.local/share/muse/sessions/2026/09/14/01a0a091-234a-7b42-9058-66de9fa99850`),
so I scanned its `session.jsonl` myself rather than trusting the commit
message's summary. It contains, in order: `retry_scheduled` facet
`{attempt:1,next_attempt:2,max_attempts:10,retry_delay_ms:1000,error_kind:"rate_limited",http_status:429}`,
`retry_scheduled` facet
`{attempt:2,next_attempt:3,max_attempts:10,retry_delay_ms:2000,error_kind:"rate_limited",http_status:429}`,
`stream_succeeded` facet `{attempt:3,max_attempts:10}`, and the owning run's
own `event.kind:"terminal"` record carries `terminal:"completed"` -- an exact
match to the commit message's claim, confirmed from the raw transcript rather
than the prose describing it.

**One correction this re-verification found that the original assessment
could not have known**: that same session's `model_completed` event carries
`model:"muse-spark-1.2"` -- not `"muse-spark-1.3-contributor"`, the value
this assessment had provisionally pinned from unrelated real-production
sessions on this machine. The reason is structural, not incidental: the
mock's `streamHappyPath` hardcodes `model := "muse-spark-1.2"` in every SSE
response object it emits, and muse's own `model_completed` event appears to
echo the provider's response rather than the client's request, so ANY
recording made against this exact mock will report `muse-spark-1.2`,
regardless of which model the driver's settings nominally select. `model` in
expected.jsonl below is corrected to `"muse-spark-1.2"` accordingly -- this is
exactly the "don't pin a doc-guessed model" rule the assess skill states,
applied one level deeper: the ORIGINAL pin wasn't doc-guessed, it was drawn
from real corpus data, but that data was against the real Meta endpoint, not
this mock, and the two diverge.

The driver side is unchanged from the original assessment and was
reconfirmed by re-reading `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh`:
`BASE_URL` is still read from `$SETTINGS_PATH` via `jq -r '.base_url //
empty'` and `spawn_muse_repl` still appends `--base-url "$BASE_URL"`.

### What changed in the recipe

The recipe now declares a machine-checkable `.mock` block
(`package`/`port`/`args`/`request_log_pattern`) per
`tools/onboarding-factory/scripts/lib/recipe-runtime.sh`'s schema, so
`record`'s `run-cell.sh` builds and launches the mock itself as a pre-driver
step (confirmed by reading `start_recipe_mock` in `run-cell.sh`) instead of
this being prose in `preconditions` for a human to do by hand. `route` flips
from `record-known-failing` to `record`; `known_failing` is removed from
expected.jsonl's meta line.
caveats: UNVERIFIED: backoff schedule beyond attempt 2. Captured examples show attempt 1->2 retry_delay_ms of 5000 (rate_limited/429) and 1000 (server/504); no example of attempt 2->3 or later exists in the local corpus, so whether the ladder is constant-delay, linear, or exponential beyond the second attempt is unconfirmed. This matters for sizing the recipe's timeout_seconds and the retry_window phase's max_delay_ms once a real recording is attempted with succeed-after > 1.

cost_nonzero asserted false: no dollar cost is persisted anywhere for muse (established machine-wide fact, muse-spark-* absent from the pricing catalog -- not re-derived here). tokens_nonzero asserted TRUE (unlike the 2-14/2-23 siblings): this scenario's turn DOES eventually succeed, so a real `model_completed` event with non-zero usage will exist for the successful attempt -- confirmed structurally by the captured `stream_succeeded` status records always being followed by the task's own `completed` event in every local example.

UNVERIFIED (carried forward, unresolved by this re-assessment): backoff schedule beyond attempt 2. The live E2E session (01a0a091-...) shows retry_delay_ms 1000 then 2000 for attempts 1->2 and 2->3 -- consistent with muse's own client-side backoff policy, not something the mock controls (the mock returns a bare status code with no Retry-After header) -- but no local example carries an attempt 3->4 or later, so whether the ladder continues linear, becomes exponential, or is capped beyond attempt 2 remains unconfirmed. Immaterial to this recipe (default --succeed-after 2 only exercises attempts 1-3), noted for anyone tuning N higher.

model is pinned to "muse-spark-1.2" -- corrected from this assessment's original "muse-spark-1.3-contributor" pin (drawn from real-production corpus sessions against the real Meta endpoint). A mock-driven recording will instead show whatever model tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-muse-overload/main.go's streamHappyPath hardcodes (currently "muse-spark-1.2", see its `const model` line) -- confirmed against the live E2E session's own model_completed record, not a doc guess. If the mock's hardcoded model ever changes, this pin goes stale with it; record should reconfirm against its own recording per the assess skill's standing rule.

cost_nonzero stays false and tokens_nonzero stays true (unchanged from the original assessment) -- re-confirmed structurally against the live E2E session's own usage object ({"input_tokens":12,"output_tokens":1,...}), not merely re-asserted.
